definition: The Identifier-Locator Network Protocol, an experimental enhancement to IP that separates a node's stable identifier from the locators used to reach it. A node may hold several locators at once, and the set changes when it moves or multihomes. RFC 6740 gives the architecture and RFC 6743 the message ILNPv6 nodes use to advertise those changes.
plainLanguage: A way of giving a computer a permanent name while letting the addresses that reach it change, so a conversation survives a move.
